title: `arg_min`, `arg_max`: the first index of a tie in memory and in a list, any tied row on streaming
verdict: in memory and `list.arg_*`: the first of tied rows; streaming column-level: any of them
description: `arg_max` over 1, 3, 3, 1 is 1 and `arg_min` is 0 in memory: the first of the tied rows. On streaming the column-level `arg_max`/`arg_min` pick any tied row, since each morsel has its own first and the morsels merge in the threads' order: with 2 threads `arg_max` was 2 (the second 3). The per-list form (`list.arg_max`, `list.arg_min`) works within one row's list, which no morsel splits, and keeps the first. NaN is skipped (polars-min-max-nan).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

The observation `df(x=[1, 3, 3, 1]).select(arg_max, arg_min).rows()` on the streaming engine gave `[(2, 3)]` with `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2` (in memory `[(1, 0)]`), where the recorded run on 10 cores gave `[(1, 0)]`: the earlier round's 'streaming gives what in memory gives' holds for that machine only. The ledger job failed on the 2-thread AWS runner (ci.yml `route`, self-hosted linux x64) over a neighbouring observation; this result was reproduced locally on macOS arm64 (Apple M4) by limiting the threads, Polars 2.1.0 (Python), not on the runner itself.
The translator uses only the per-list form (`engine.py`, `greatest`/`least`), which morsels do not split, so no lowered plan changes; the reference's `tie_pick` allows any tied row.
